name: Least-Privilege Identity & Access Management
summary: Grant an AI workload's service identity only the specific permissions it needs — nothing broader — and prefer short-lived, scoped credentials over standing access.

source.title: Least-privilege access — common cloud security guidance
source.reference: Consistent guidance across Microsoft Entra ID, AWS IAM, and Google Cloud IAM documentation.

name: Encryption at Rest and in Transit
summary: Encrypt stored data (documents, embeddings, logs) and data in motion between services, using platform-managed or customer-managed keys depending on compliance requirements.

source.title: Data encryption — common cloud security baseline
source.reference: Baseline guidance shared across Microsoft, AWS, and Google Cloud security documentation.

name: Azure AI Content Safety
summary: A managed service that screens model input and output for harmful content categories (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual content) and supports custom blocklists.

source.title: Azure AI Content Safety documentation
source.reference: Microsoft Learn — Azure AI Content Safety.

name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
summary: Configurable policies that filter denied topics, harmful content, and sensitive information (e.g. PII) in both prompts and model responses, applied consistently across models used through Bedrock.

name: Prompt Injection Mitigation
summary: Layered defenses against malicious instructions embedded in retrieved content or user input — input/output filtering, privilege separation between trusted and untrusted content, and human confirmation before high-impact actions.

source.title: LLM Top 10 — Prompt Injection
source.reference: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications.

name: Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gates
summary: Require explicit human review and approval before an agent takes a high-impact or irreversible action, rather than allowing fully autonomous execution.

source.title: Human oversight in agentic systems
source.reference: Anthropic engineering guidance on agent safety and human oversight.

name: Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMK)
summary: Use keys the customer controls (rather than platform-managed keys) to encrypt data at rest, so the organization — not the cloud vendor — controls key rotation and revocation for regulated workloads.

source.title: Customer-managed keys — common cloud security guidance
source.reference: Consistent guidance across Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, and Google Cloud KMS documentation.
